nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which organizations or authors are referenced in relation to the impacts of waste management?
nodes.answer: The paragraph references Parveen et al. (2023) for direct and indirect impacts, and UNEP (2023) regarding the global agenda of waste management.
nodes.paragraph: Keywords Local knowledge Waste management Sustainable communities Socio-ecological systems framework Integrated sustainable approach Botswana * Isabella P. Ntsabane ipmakgatswana@gmail.com Kgosietsile Velempini velempinik@uncw.edu Hesekia Garekae Garekaeh@ub.ac.bw Pulane Koosaletse-Mswela Mswelap@ub.ac.bw 1 Environmental Education Unit, Languages and Social Science Education Department, Faculty of Education, University of Botswana, Gaborone, Botswana 2 Department of Environmental Sciences, University of North Carolina Wilmington, Wilmington, USA 3 Department of Environmental Science, Faculty of Sciences, University of Botswana, Gaborone, Botswana 4 Department of Range and Forest Resources, Botswana University of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Gaborone, Botswana 58 Socio-Ecological Practice Research (2025) 7:57 76 1 Introduction Waste management has both direct and indirect environ- mental impacts, which include land occupation, resource depletion, global warming, water pollution and cytotoxic effects from air emissions (Parveen et al. 2023, p. ix). Waste is important in the global agenda because it affects each one of the United Nations triple planetary crisis of climate change, nature and biodiversity, and pollution and waste (UNEP 2023, p. 2 of 15).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Partnerships for the goals|Global sustainability regulation|Waste management guidelines_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What are the subsequent sections outlined after the introduction of waste management practices?
nodes.answer: The following sections include a description of the waste management situation in Botswana, theoretical views guiding the study, methodology explanation, findings presentation, discussion, conclusions, and recommendations.
nodes.paragraph: For practition- ers, this new knowledge adds to the inventory of sustainable waste management practices available to local communi- ties. This inventory will serve as a starting point for scholars evaluating the sustainability of identified waste management practices. The identified practices could also be tested for applicability in similar settings. In the next section, we present waste management situ- ation in Botswana, sub-Saharan Africa region, ending with a description of the study area. In the following section, we expound on theoretical views that guided the study, followed by an explanation of the methodology used. After that, we present the findings, followed by a discussion. Lastly, con- clusions drawn from the study and recommendations are provided. 2 Waste management in Botswana, sub Saharan Africa region Literature review highlights successful case studies of the application of local knowledge on waste management in sub- Saharan Africa. These studies underscore the relevance of local knowledge in solid waste management. For example, Burkina Faso demonstrated transition from centralized com- posting to individual on site pits within their homes (Kaza et al. 2018, p. 152).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Partnerships for the goals|Global sustainability regulation|Waste management guidelines_qna_002
nodes.label: Ethics and Regulation
nodes.question: What do international recommendations emphasize in relation to EHS risks associated with waste management?
nodes.answer: International recommendations emphasize the prevention and precaution of EHS risks associated with waste management to protect human health and the environment.
